listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, October 12, 2026. The lead story is from Atlanta. One person has died and four others were injured after an incident on the Goliath rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. Atlanta media outlets said the victim was ejected from the ride. The coaster was shut down after the accident. Details have not been released. Now the front page. Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack and is ignoring the energy ceasefire that President Trump declared. In France, a fourteen-year-old was detained after the middle-school principal and a teacher were injured in a shooting at a school. The Atlanta Dream beat the New York Liberty eighty-five to eighty-three to complete a three-game sweep, and they now face the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals. Federal agents searched the Washington home of Representative Ilhan Omar. The Justice Department says the warrant was approved as part of an ongoing federal investigation. Omar calls it an attempt to target political enemies. In sports, Rockets coverage looks at Cooper Flagg's growth after the NBA China Games. The 49ers say wide receiver Deebo Samuel is expected to miss at least a couple of weeks with a hamstring injury. In UFC, Andre Fili won with a first-round knockout. In Tech and AI, Claude Platform added dynamic workflows for Managed Agents in beta. In politics, Drop Site News covers the Iran situation and the Strait of Hormuz. In world news, Saudi Arabia's minister vowed a serious response after Houthi attacks hit Riyadh's airport, killing thirteen people. In Atlanta, a Gwinnett County campus project is taking its first steps, and a new office tower on Northside Drive is changing the skyline. In architecture, Hexagon will acquire Rocscience for five hundred thirty-five million dollars. In science, Chinook salmon are returning to the Klamath River after four dams were removed. NASA's picture of the day shows Jupiter and its moons. Researchers are also studying how scarred blood vessels may help explain Alzheimer's risk linked to the APOE4 gene. That is the brief. Have a good day.

The park is in the Atlanta area, so this is close to home for you. The summary does not yet say what caused the incident, so further reporting will be needed to explain it.
